keyFindings.title: A plugin `bin/` directory is also added to the Bash tool's `PATH` while the plugin is enabled, according to the [Claude Code plugin manifest reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference). keyFindings.title: Preview data is outside `structuredContent` today. `previewFrom` converts the JPEG buffer to a base64 string in an MCP image block at `mcp server/src/tools/media/preview.ts:38-45`, and `withPreviewBlock` appends that block to `content` at lines 119-123. Both `image_probe` and `media_probe` can append the preview block at `mcp server/src/tools/image/probe.ts:139-154` and `mcp server/src/tools/media/probe.ts:361-398`. keyFindings.title: Resolver and capability caches are process-local maps. `capabilityCache` maps binary path to an in-flight or completed promise at `mcp server/src/core/capabilities.ts:163,348-386`. The resolver maps tool name to a `CacheEntry` and in-flight lookup at `mcp server/src/core/ffmpeg-resolver.ts:446-449`. Resolver hits are revalidated against file existence, size, and modification time at lines 467-485. Tests already cover capability reuse and invalidation at `mcp server/tests/core/capabilities.vitest.ts:349-420`, plus resolver reuse and size or mtime changes at `mcp server/tests/core/ffmpeg-resolver.vitest.ts:809-861`. A one-shot CLI process loses these maps on exit. Persist only validated metadata under the data directory, using atomic writes and a versioned schema. Cache keys should include platform, architecture, config overrides, PATH identity, and data directory. Re-stat cached binaries on each process start, retain pinned install hash checks for installed binaries at `mcp server/src/core/ffmpeg-resolver.ts:552-584`, do not persist misses, and invalidate on setup or failure. These persistence details are recommendations.

keyFindings.title: Signal handling needs a CLI-specific cancellation path. The MCP entry catches SIGINT and SIGTERM and closes the server at `mcp server/src/index.ts:56-88`. The process runner starts a local child in `spawnAndWait` at `mcp server/src/core/process-runner.ts:360-374`, and only its timeout path kills that child with a grace period at lines 466-479. `withTempDir` removes its folder in `finally` at lines 687-702. Proposed CLI behavior: a shared abort controller stops active children, the CLI awaits dispatch settlement so tool `finally` cleanup runs, then it exits with documented statuses. This process registry and signal-to-cancellation path are recommendations, not existing runtime behavior.

keyFindings.title: The preferred skill invocation is an explicit `node` command whose script path contains `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, for example `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/server/dist/cli.js"`. Claude Code substitutes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in plugin skill Markdown and in the skill's `allowed-tools` rules. It is not an environment variable available to commands launched by the Bash tool. keyFindings.title: Tool definitions contain a Zod input shape and metadata. `listedInputSchema` adds `fileName` and `subfolder` when output placement applies, and the registry publishes title, description, schema, and annotations at `mcp server/src/server/tool-registry.ts:91-99,129-139`. Zod is already a direct dependency at `mcp server/package.json:24-29`, and the installed Zod v4 type exposes `toJSONSchema` at `mcp server/node_modules/zod/v4/classic/schemas.d.ts:7-18`. Recommended `describe <tool>` implementation: resolve the name in `ALL_TOOLS`, build `z.object(listedInputSchema(definition))`, and call `toJSONSchema()` so placement parameters appear in the caller-facing schema. `list` should emit the existing tool order with name, title, and description. This does not require a second JSON Schema dependency.
